sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: canceling 'stops the Dataflow service from processing any data, including buffered data' and 'You might lose in-flight data when you cancel a job'; draining (streaming only) 'enables the Dataflow service to finish processing the buffered data while simultaneously ceasing the ingestion of new data'; on drain, Dataflow 'immediately closes any in-process windows and fires all triggers'.

sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (a third-party explanation, to verify against the Apache Beam programming guide). Relevant text: 'By default late events are rejected from the window'; data arriving after the end of the window and of the allowed lateness is 'droppable late data'; withAllowedLateness 'defines how long late data will be accepted'; its example accepts a late element with accumulating fired panes and fires a later pane. The droppedDueToLateness counter name in the scenario is from memory of Beam (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the data engineer for Larchfield Taxis, a fictional ride-hailing company. The streaming Dataflow job fares-per-minute reads ride-completed events from Pub/Sub and writes per-minute fare totals, by ride end time, to the BigQuery table fares_minute. Finance reconciles them with the payment processor at 16:00 and has flagged that BigQuery has been about 4% low every day since Monday.
handover: Monday's driver app release queues rides completed without signal and sends them when the phone reconnects.
Every raw event is also archived to the BigQuery table rides_raw by a separate subscription.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows Pub/Sub, the streaming job's windows, the raw archive and the totals table.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the totals were short, what you changed in the windowing and why that much, and how the past days were corrected.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Ties the shortfall to late data and the window's lateness setting.
parts.modelAnswer: Since Monday's release, rides completed offline arrive late; the job's one-minute event-time windows had no allowed lateness, so the windowing step dropped about 41,000 late events, 3.8% of fares.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Sizes allowed lateness from the measured delay and replaces the job without losing data.
parts.modelAnswer: Measured lateness: p99 18 minutes, maximum 25, so allowed lateness is 30 minutes with a late trigger and accumulating panes merged by window into BigQuery. The old job was drained, not cancelled, so its buffered data was finished. Processing-time windows would have hidden the drops by putting fares in the wrong minute.

parts.label: Past days
parts.criteria: Recomputes history from the raw archive and checks the reconciliation.
parts.modelAnswer: A batch job over rides_raw recomputed every minute since Monday by ride end time; the reconciliation for Monday and today shows 0.0% before 16:00.

expertPath.text: Reconciliation: -3.8% from Monday; the drop counter: about 41,000 late events; the code: no allowed lateness; arrival delay p99 18 min, max 25.
Drain and replace with 30 minutes of allowed lateness and accumulating late panes; start the backfill from rides_raw.
The new job is running and the backfill finishes; Monday and today reconcile at 0.0%.

dataLost.headline: Fixing data loss by losing data
dataLost.body: Cancel stops a job at once, buffered data included. Drain stops reading, finishes what the job holds and fires its windows, so a replacement can start from the subscription without a gap.

reconMissed.headline: The reconciliation failed again
reconMissed.body: Two things are needed: allowed lateness so new late events count, and a backfill from the raw archive for the days already lost. Workers change neither.

reconciled.headline: Good: event time, with room for late data
reconciled.body: You found the drops, measured how late the data really is, sized allowed lateness from it, replaced the job without losing buffered data, recomputed the lost days from the archive, and reconciled before 16:00.

gaps.headline: Reconciled, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: reading the drop counter, measuring the delays, the reconciliation check, or a change that did not help.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The shortfall began with Monday's release, which queues rides completed offline and sends them late. The job windows by ride end time into one-minute windows with no allowed lateness, and its drop counter shows about 41,000 events discarded as late. Measure how late the data is (p99 18 minutes, maximum 25), set allowed lateness to 30 minutes with a late trigger and accumulating panes merged by window, and replace the job by draining it so its buffered data is finished; cancelling would lose that data. Processing-time windows would put fares in the wrong minute, and more workers do not change lateness. Recompute Monday to now from the raw archive with a batch job, then reconcile before 16:00.
